cognate: ձեռն ~ χέρας continues *ǵhes- hand; գործ ~ ἔργον continues *werg̑- work.
drift_or_renewal: Placement verbs renewed: Armenian արկեալ, participle of arkanem cast/put, versus Greek ἵεσαν, imperfect of hiēmi send; singular versus plural hand.
shared_syntax: Accusative hand as object of cast/send, with directional preposition plus accusative work: put/send hands to work.
context: Armenian attendants begin gathering martyrs remains into baskets; Greek attendants begin sacrificial preparations. Both introduce coordinated manual ritual service, using the same directional hand-to-work idiom. A second Armenian slab witness applies the same idiom to whatever enterprise Vahan undertakes, confirming idiomatic usage outside relic collection.
qualification: Two cognate nouns in the same nonliteral directional construction make this more specific than simple work done by hands. Still a transparent idiom: independent innovation and Greek influence on Christian Armenian are substantial alternatives. Corpus-index hand/work search mostly yielded unrelated genitive/instrumental expressions; no third-branch confirmation.
